Activist Sonam Wangchuk has voiced support for the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) protest in Delhi, describing the situation in India as an “undeclared Emergency” after several protesters and leaders, including CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, were detained on October 10.
Wangchuk, who did not attend the protest at Jantar Mantar, warned that he would consider launching a hunger strike or a foot march if those detained were not released by the following day. His remarks came a day after he explained his decision to stay in Ladakh, citing important work at home.
"India in a state of undeclared Emergency," Wangchuk said in a post on X, criticising the mass detentions.
"I will be compelled to consider an Anshan Fast (hunger strike) or Padyatra March (foot march) if they are not released by tomorrow," he added.
The CJP and Opposition leaders had sought to protest in New Delhi over alleged electoral irregularities and what they described as “collusion” between the Election Commission and the ruling BJP. They were, however, disallowed from holding the demonstration at Jantar Mantar.

LIVE
Background
CJP Delhi Protest Live Update: Authorities in Delhi have stepped up security measures ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10. The measures include prohibitory orders, denial of permission for the demonstration and a request to restrict access to 57 metro stations.
The Delhi Police have imposed Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the New Delhi district, restricting the assembly of more than five people. Police have also denied permission for the protest called by the CJP and some student organisations.
Joint Commissioner of Police, New Delhi Range, Nupur Prasad, said on Friday that the application seeking permission was received on October 7, just three days before the planned demonstration. According to police guidelines, applications must be submitted at least 10 days in advance.
Delhi Police Seek Restrictions At 57 Metro Stations
The Delhi Police have also asked the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to shut 57 metro stations from 9 pm on Friday until Saturday, citing the possibility of an "unruly mob movement towards sensitive locations".
In a letter sent on Thursday, Joint Commissioner of Police (Transport Range) Rajneesh Gupta said the frequency of metro trains passing through these stations could also be reduced on October 10, depending on the situation. The proposed restrictions are linked to the planned CJP protest at Jantar Mantar.
The stations listed in the request include Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, Kashmere Gate, Chandni Chowk, INA, Hauz Khas, Azadpur, Jamia Millia Islamia, Shaheen Bagh, Welcome and Rohini West.
CJP Protest Targets CEC Over SIR Allegations
The CJP has called the demonstration against Kumar over allegations of voter-list tampering during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The allegations also concern claims that the CEC bypassed his two colleagues to make changes involving Form 6, which is used to register as a voter.

Indian police crackdown appears to have prevented mass protests against the country’s election chief from taking place.
Police in India’s capital New Delhi have detained more than 1,000 protesters, opposition politicians, journalists, student union leaders, lawyers and the founders of the “Cockroach” youth movement in an effort to quash their demonstration demanding the resignation of the election chief.
The satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other youth groups had announced a protest in the subcontinent’s capital for Saturday, aimed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of India’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
The protesters accuse the governing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using the SIR to sway election results, in collusion with its appointees in the election commission, including Kumar.
Meanwhile, opposition parties say the voter deletions also affected the outcome of some recent state elections won by the BJP, and have cast a shadow on elections in the world’s largest democracy.
The CJP had planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in central Delhi.
But on Saturday, the area was sealed off by security forces before the demonstration began.
The Indian capital was also in lockdown with thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed across the city, trains to New Delhi cancelled, mobile internet services suspended and metro stations and markets shuttered, in an effort to stop the protests.
BJP spokesman Sambit Patra has dismissed the demonstrators as “anarchic elements”.
“Their flop show has been completely demolished,” Patra said. “What is happening at Jantar Mantar, what you can see on TV and a few social media handles, is not India’s story. India is calm and going ahead under good governance,” he told reporters.

'Cockroach' group leaders among hundreds detained in Delhi protest

Hundreds of protesters have reportedly been detained in Delhi during the latest demonstration by the Gen-Z led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over electoral reforms.
The group said its founder Abhijeet Dipke, who began the movement in May after India's Chief Justice likened some jobless young people to "cockroaches", was detained with other leaders shortly after landing in Delhi.
Tens of thousands of security personnel were deployed and roads barricaded ahead of the demonstration, though the CJP insisted it would go ahead.
Delhi Police has not commented on the detentions, but had refused permission for the protest to take place at Jantar Mantar, a landmark in the Indian capital.
The group - who are not registered as a political party in India - are seeking electoral reforms just months before crucial state elections.
It has also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters' lists - which the Election Commission has denied.
Under Kumar's leadership, India's election commission has undertaken a mammoth exercise to update electoral rolls nationwide - it said this was a routine exercise to weed out dead, duplicate or ineligible voters.
But in many states, the exercise has been shrouded in controversy, with tens of thousands of people alleging they have been wrongly removed.
The CJP - and opposition parties - accuse Kumar of favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the way the electoral rolls are being updated.
The Election Commission and the BJP have denied this.
Before arriving in Delhi, the CJP's founder Dipke said: "If you think you can stop us by threatening us with jail or trying to intimidate us with the fear of imprisonment, you are mistaken."
He and and two other leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained on their flight from Mumbai on Saturday.
The group claimed the three men have been taken to an undisclosed location. Delhi Police have not commented.
Ajinkya Shinde, the CJP's new designated leader while the others are in detention, released a video telling protesters that "if Delhi Police tries to stop you, wherever they stop you will become your Jantar Mantar".
Student activist Neha Bora, who had also been detained by Delhi Police, urged demonstrators to "hold the line".

फ्लाइट के अंदर से एक वीडियो सामने आया है। इसमें महिला पुलिसकर्मी दीपके और CJP के दूसरे नेताओं को हिरासत में लेते दिख रही हैं।
दो मिनट के वीडियो में क्या-क्या हुआ…
वीडियो में दीपके कहते सुनाई देते हैं, “आप देख सकते हैं कि देश किस दिशा में जा रहा है। हमें फ्लाइट में ही हिरासत में लिया जा रहा है। ऐसा तो कभी इंदिरा गांधी ने भी नहीं किया था। यह तानाशाही है, लेकिन हम इनसे डरते नहीं हैं।”
दीपके पुलिसकर्मियों की ओर इशारा करते हुए कहते हैं, “आओ, हमें गिरफ्तार कर लो। हम गिरफ्तार होने ही आए हैं। मैं आपसे डरता नहीं हूं। हम गिरफ्तारी के लिए तैयार हैं।”
इस पर एक पुलिसकर्मी जवाब देती हैं, “नहीं, यह गिरफ्तारी नहीं है। सर, कृपया कॉपरेट करें।”
इसके बाद दीपके और फ्लाइट में बैठे उनके साथियों ने ‘भारत माता की जय’ के नारे लगाए। दीपके ने ‘इंकलाब जिंदाबाद’ के नारे भी लगाए।
फ्लाइट में महिला पुलिसकर्मी आगे खड़ी थीं। दीपके ने उनसे कहा, “आप लोग फ्लाइट में कैसे आ गए?” वहीं, पुलिसकर्मी उनसे बाहर आने के लिए कहती रहीं।
आशुतोष और दीपके ने पुलिस से पुरुष पुलिसकर्मियों को आगे करने के लिए कहा। इस पर महिला पुलिसकर्मी उनसे बाहर आने का अनुरोध करती रहीं।
आशुतोष और सौरभ दास के बाद महिला पुलिसकर्मियों ने दीपके को बाहर ले जाने की कोशिश की। इस दौरान दीपके ने हाथ जोड़कर कहा, “मुझे अपना फोन तो लेने दीजिए। मैं अपना बैग ले लूं। मैं गिरफ्तार होने ही आया हूं।”
इसके बाद पुलिस दीपके और उनके साथियों को फ्लाइट से बाहर ले गई। इस दौरान दीपके कहते सुनाई दिए, “कौन-सी जेल में डालोगे? राजस्थान की? NSA या UAPA, जो लगाना है लगाओ।”

corpus.title: India cracks down on youth ‘Cockroach’ movement as anger grows against Modi, election chief
corpus.signal_text:
Indian authorities deployed a sweeping security crackdown across New Delhi and detained thousands of protesters Saturday as India’s youth “Cockroach” movement sought to intensify a nationwide campaign against a contentious voter list revision that has fuelled anger at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government and election authorities.
Police moved to break up the demonstration before it could begin, intercepting demonstrators on their way to Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in the heart of India’s capital, chasing off some and detaining many others. Some were dragged away before being bundled into police vehicles and taken to temporary detention centers. Several “Cockroach” movement leaders, opposition lawmakers and student activists were detained before arriving, effectively crippling the protest ahead of its start.
Indian police detain several people in ‘Cockroach’ youth protests against voter roll changes
The crackdown extended beyond the protest venue, with police stopping buses, cars and other vehicles at checkpoints on routes into the capital and searching for demonstrators. Jantar Mantar was barricaded, while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear gas launchers were stationed along key routes. Restrictions on mobile internet and access to parts of the city added to the hurdles facing protesters.
Police said Friday they had denied permission for the protest because the request was submitted late.
Sambit Patra, a spokesperson for Modi’s party, dismissed the demonstrators as “anarchic elements.”
“Their flop show has been completely demolished,” Patra said.
The scale of the crackdown underscored the authorities’ determination to disrupt a fast-growing protest campaign that has mobilized thousands of young people, drawn opposition support and intensified scrutiny of Modi. The protests also come at a politically sensitive time, months after demonstrations led by the “Cockroach” movement over exam paper leaks forced Modi’s education minister to resign in July.

Leaders of the “Cockroach” movement Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were expected to be at the forefront of the protest, were detained after arriving at Delhi airport from Mumbai on Saturday. A video shared by the “Cockroach Janta Party” on X showed police boarding the aircraft and detaining the three men.

corpus.title: No trains, no UPI: Rail passengers in Delhi face CJP protest pain
corpus.signal_text:
No trains, no internet for UPI: Rail passengers in Delhi face CJP protest pain
The public announcement system at the New Delhi Railway Station was busy announcing one train cancellation after another. The suspension of mobile internet meant no UPI and no news updates. Railway passengers were caught in the crossfire as the Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest and the security clampdown left them stranded far from home without a Plan B.
The heat was unforgiving in the national capital, the trains were cancelled, and even a lemon soda came with an unexpected problem. At New Delhi Railway Station on Saturday, 23-year-old Abhinav had one more thing to worry about after finding out that he had forgotten his wallet. With internet services suspended, completing a UPI payment for the drink he had already consumed became a struggle.
"I forgot to carry my wallet and now, with no mobile internet, payments through mobile are also not possible," Abhinav told India Today Digital.
The Varanasi-bound commuter said he realised he had left his wallet behind only after buying the drink. And just when he thought he could wait for his train, another announcement dashed his hopes. The train he was supposed to board had been cancelled, leaving him waiting at the station until after 2 pm.
For Abhinav, and hundreds of other rail commuters in the national capital, it was a total disruption.
The disruptions at New Delhi Railway Station and Hazrat Nijamuddin Railway Station were part of a wider security clampdown in the national capital amid the proposed demonstration by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP). The CJP is protesting, seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged issues related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise of voter rolls.
Across the station, announcements in Hindi continued to echo through the speakers. "Varanasi ke liye jaane waali train radhh ki jayi hai (The train to Varanasi has been cancelled)." Another announcement followed, informing passengers that the Pune Express had also been cancelled.
These were not isolated announcements. More than 170 trains had been cancelled for the day, a railway official at New Delhi Railway Station, speaking on condition of anonymity, told India Today Digital.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has made 221 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF), comprising around 23,000 personnel, available to the Delhi Police from October 8 to 12. corpus.title: 'Kya aap Emergency dekh sakte hain?' CJP reacts as politicians, journalists, lawyers detained
corpus.signal_text:
Image Credit: X/@Cockroachisback, ANI. CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke detained by the Police at Delhi Airport.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) took a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday, calling the police action against protesters an "emergency"-like situation. Police detained protesters, activists, journalists and lawyers ahead of the party’s ‘Delhi Chalo’ march. Hundreds of people were stopped across Delhi as organisers planned to gather at Jantar Mantar and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over disputed voter-roll revisions.
"Kya aap Emergency dekh sakte hain, fraands?" the CJP asked in a satirical response to the detentions. The remark invoked India's 1975-77 Emergency, when civil liberties were severely curtailed and opposition leaders were jailed under then-Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
- Protestors Detained - Politicians Detained - Journalists Detained - Lawyers Detained https://t.co/LViLfBLEPx
— Cockroach Janta Party - CJP (@Cockroachisback) October 10, 2026
Police have detained about 200 more protesters in Connaught Place while attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, News Agency ANI reported earlier, quoting Delhi Police sources. Earlier, police had reported detaining roughly 500 people travelling in groups towards the demonstration.
Police also said nearly 50 people with criminal antecedents were taken into preventive custody, separate from those identified as protesters. The New Delhi district was divided into 20 operational zones, with temporary detention centres established for each. Stadiums were also designated for holding detainees.
Police said the march had not received permission. Authorities cited public order concerns and said the organisers' application was filed too close to the protest date. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were in force. Roadblocks, metro closures and restrictions on mobile internet disrupted movement in central Delhi.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, who travelled from Mumbai, was detained after his flight landed at Delhi airport. Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were also held. In a video shared on Instagram, Dipke alleged that officers had boarded the aircraft before passengers disembarked.
"Not even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency," he said, accusing the authorities of treating peaceful protesters like criminals. "We are not afraid of you," he added.

Delhi Police detained student leader Neha Bora and several protesters on Saturday as demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar spread to other parts of the capital. Meanwhile, Delhi airport authorities detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two colleagues. Police said the protest had not received permission.
Earlier, Bora, the national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA), called on supporters to gather elsewhere after police blocked access to Jantar Mantar. "Dilli Haat becomes our Jantar Mantar! Gyanesh Kumar must go!" she wrote on X.
Dilli Haat becomes our Jantar Mantar! Gyanesh Kumar must go! https://t.co/T33Q8uz4iB
— Neha (@neha_aisa) October 10, 2026
Earlier today, at Indira Gandhi International Airport, police officers boarded a flight from Mumbai and detained CJP founder Dipke along with senior leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Videos shared by the group showed officers confronting the activists before escorting them away.
NCP (SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande, who was travelling on the same flight, said he did not know where the three had been taken.
"We were all on the same flight. The three of them were sitting right in front of me. Police officers entered the aircraft, inconvenienced all other passengers and picked him up from the aircraft. We do not even know whether he (Dipke) has been brought out of the airport or is still there," he told reporters.
Gawande said protesters were still attempting to reach Jantar Mantar and urged police to exercise restraint.
"The plan will be revealed to you very soon. Currently, young people are making their way to Jantar Mantar. We hope that the Police will not use excessive violence or force. We hope that the Police will treat young people of this country as equal citizens, rather than criminals who deserve to be punished," he said.
Police deployed thousands of personnel and set up barricades and vehicle checkpoints around central Delhi. Authorities restricted access to dozens of Metro stations, disrupted some rail services and suspended mobile internet in parts of the city.
Delhi Police said the organisers had submitted their application too late to meet the required notice period. Officers also cited prohibitory orders and public-order concerns.
